questions.q: What's the minimal code difference between writing plain Parquet and writing Delta?
options: Adding .format("delta") to the write call — the underlying data files still look like ordinary Parquet
Delta requires an entirely separate write API with no relation to spark.write
Delta tables cannot be written using PySpark at all
Parquet writes require .format("delta") too, so there's no real difference
questions.explain: This makes Lesson 13's point — Delta is Parquet underneath — completely literal.

questions.q: Why does DESCRIBE HISTORY have no equivalent for a plain Parquet folder?
options: A plain Parquet folder has no transaction log at all to ask about — DESCRIBE HISTORY reads directly from _delta_log/
DESCRIBE HISTORY works identically on both, so this isn't actually true
Parquet files don't support any kind of read query
DESCRIBE HISTORY only works with CSV files, not Parquet or Delta
questions.explain: Every version, every operation, every timestamp — all sourced from the log Lesson 13 introduced.

questions.q: What happens when two jobs write to the same plain Parquet folder at the same time?
options: There's a real risk of half-written, inconsistent files, since Parquet writes aren't atomic
Spark automatically queues the writes so only one runs at a time
The second write is always silently ignored
Nothing unusual happens — Parquet handles concurrent writes safely by default
questions.explain: This is exactly the atomicity gap Delta Lake's transaction log closes.

questions.q: What happens when two jobs write to the same Delta table at the same time?
options: Delta's transaction log resolves the conflict — one write succeeds cleanly, or fails cleanly, never half-written
Both writes always fail immediately with no data written
The two writes are automatically merged together, regardless of content
Delta tables cannot be written to concurrently under any circumstances
questions.explain: This is the direct, practical payoff of the atomicity guarantee Delta's log provides.

questions.q: Once a Delta table is loaded into a DataFrame, how does working with it compare to a Parquet-based DataFrame?
options: Completely unchanged — select, filter, groupBy, joins from Foundations' Chapter 4 all work identically on either one
Delta DataFrames require an entirely different set of PySpark methods
Delta DataFrames cannot be filtered or joined at all
Only SQL can be used on a Delta-backed DataFrame, never the DataFrame API
questions.explain: Delta changes how safely the data got written and how much history you can ask about — not how you work with it once loaded.
